note_title: 把积分或求和对象视为一个计数函数并展开

callouts.id: 把积分或求和对象视为一个计数函数并展开#1
callouts.title: 想法0
callouts.body:
当我们要估计或计算一个积分$\int XY$或和$\sum XY$遇到困难时，并且：
1. $Y$难以做常规的积分或求和处理。
2. $Y$可以被看成是某种计数函数，即存在一个条件$\text{cond}$，使得$$Y=\sum 1_{\text{cond}}$$
那么值得尝试把$Y$当计数函做和的展开，然后交换次序变成$$\sum \int X\cdot1_{\text{cond}}\quad \text{or}\quad \sum \sum X\cdot1_{\text{cond}}$$

如果$\int X\cdot1_{\text{cond}}$或$\sum X\cdot1_{\text{cond}}$是容易直接估计或计算的对象，或者借助[[把条件函数展开为新的和或积分然后换序]]的思路从而变得好处理的多项，那么这个思路就算是一定程度上简化了原有的积分或和的计算（或估计）问题。

if_strategy_template.strategy_name_en: Treat the Integrand or Summand as a Counting Function and Expand
if_strategy_template.summary_en: When an integral like $\int XY$ or a sum like $\sum XY$ is hard to handle because $Y$ is awkward, try expressing $Y$ as a counting function of the form $Y=\sum 1_{\text{cond}}$. Then expand and interchange the order to reduce the problem to simpler integrals or sums involving indicator functions.
if_strategy_template.applicability: Applies when one factor in an integral or sum can be rewritten as a count of how many conditions are satisfied, and the resulting terms after exchanging order are easier to estimate or compute.

callouts.body:
对于$\text{Re}(s)>1$，定义
$$ \zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}$$
证明：$$ \zeta(s) = s \int_{1}^{\infty} \frac{[x]}{x^{s+1}} \, dx $$

callouts.id: 把积分或求和对象视为一个计数函数并展开#4
callouts.title: 例子3.1:指数的Legendre公式的证明
callouts.body:
在[[从二项式系数到Kummer定理#1. Legendre公式]]当中我们介绍了计算阶乘$n!$素因子$p$指数的办法$$
u_p(n!)=\sum_{k\geq 1}\left\lfloor rac{n}{p^k}ightfloor$$我们可以试着从本篇文章当中的观点中来证明这件事。我们利用$$
u_p(r_1r_2)=
u_p(r_1)+
u_p(r_2)$$的这种性质。那么$$
u_p(n!)=\sum_{m=1}^n 
u_p(m)$$其中我们把$
u_p(m)$视为一个计数函数，即$$
u_p(m)=\sum_{k\geq 1}1_{p^k|m}$$从而带入到$
u_p(n!)$的式子当中，并交换求和次序，从而得到$$
u_p(n!)=\sum_{m=1}^n \sum_{k\geq 1}1_{p^k|m}= \sum_{k\geq 1}\sum_{m=1}^n1_{p^k|m}=\sum_{k\geq 1}\left\lfloor  rac{n}{p^k} ightfloor$$这便是Legendre公式。

classification_result.id: 把积分或求和对象视为一个计数函数并展开#4
classification_result.english_title: Example 3.1: A Proof of Legendre's Formula for the Exponent

if_problem.statement_en:
Using the viewpoint of this note, prove Legendre's formula for the exponent of a prime $p$ in $n!$: $$
u_p(n!)=\sum_{k\geq 1}\left\lfloor rac{n}{p^k}ightfloor.$$ The argument starts from $$
u_p(n!)=\sum_{m=1}^n 
u_p(m)$$ and rewrites $$
u_p(m)=\sum_{k\geq 1}1_{p^k\mid m}.$$
key_techniques: rewrite valuation as a counting function
